plan.contextChunk:
are, essentially, inverses of each other. Many algorithms explicitly
treat them as inverse problems, where solving the problem in one
direction can inform the solution in the other direction.

In @sec-neural_nets, we described neural nets as being a
sequence of mappings from raw data to ever more abstracted
representations, layer by layer. This perspective puts representation
learning in the spotlight: deep learning is just representation
learning! Let us now point out an alternative perspective: in backward
order, deep nets are mappings from abstracted representations to ever
more concrete representations of the data, layer by layer. This backward
ordering is the direction in which deep generative networks work. This
perspective puts the spotlight on generative modeling: deep learning is
just generative modeling! Indeed both modeling directions are valid, and
the full picture looks like this
(@fig-generative_modeling_and_representation_learning-rep_gen_schematic):

![The relationship between representation learning and generative modeling. Here we label one side as "Data" and the other as "Embedding"; but what's the precise difference between these two things? Why is an RGB image data while a 100-dimensional vector of neural activations is an embedding? This is a question for you to think about; there is no correct answer.](./figures/generative_modeling_and_representation_learning/rep_gen_schematic.png){width="35%" #fig-generative_modeling_and_representation_learning-rep_gen_schematic}

:::{.column-margin}
Moving backward through a net is also what backpropagation does, but it computes a different function: backpropagation computes the gradient $\nabla f$ whereas here we focus on the inverse $f^{-1}$.
:::



## Latent Variables as Representations

In @sec-generative_models, we introduced generative models
with latent variables $\mathbf{z}$. In that context, the role of the
latent variable was to specify all unobserved factors that might affect
the output of a model. For example, if the model predicts the color of a
black and white photo, it is a mapping
$g: \mathbf{x}, \mathbf{z} \rightarrow \mathbf{y}$, with $\mathbf{x}$

elements: tall rectangular prism wireframe bounding box representing the deep network's layer space
four stacked horizontal semi-transparent gray planes representing network layers (from data layer at bottom to embedding layer at top)
five black data point spheres lying on the bottom plane ('Data')
five smooth 3D spline trajectories tracing paths from the bottom data points, winding slightly through the intermediate planes, to the top plane ('Embedding')
arrowheads on the trajectories pointing upwards for representation learning, or downwards for generative modeling
animated glowing particles traveling along the trajectories to visualize information flow
vertical text labels alongside the box: 'Representation learning' (with upward arrow) and 'Generative modeling' (with downward arrow)
horizontal text labels: 'Data' below the box, 'Embedding' above the box

interactions.label: Flow Direction
interactions.teaches: Demonstrates how representation learning maps concrete data upward into abstract embeddings, whereas generative modeling runs in reverse, mapping latent embeddings back to concrete data.

interactions.label: Inspect Layer
interactions.teaches: Slices the network at different depths to show how trajectories represent intermediate activations as data is transformed layer-by-layer.

demo_steps.title: Dual paths of deep learning
demo_steps.narration: Observe the stacked planes representing layers of a neural network. Five distinct data points at the bottom ('Data') are mapped through intermediate representations to the top plane ('Embedding'). Representation learning and generative modeling are inverse perspectives of this exact same space.

demo_steps.title: Representation learning: Bottom-to-top
demo_steps.narration: In the forward direction, raw, high-dimensional data (like image pixels) is mapped layer-by-layer into highly abstracted, low-dimensional representations. Watch the particles flow upward, losing redundant details while retaining semantic meaning.

demo_steps.title: Generative modeling: Top-to-bottom
demo_steps.narration: Now we reverse the flow. In generative modeling, we sample an abstract concept or latent vector from the embedding space and map it backward. The network progressively adds concrete detail, turning an abstract code back into realistic data at the bottom.

interactionPlan.camera_suggestion: An orthographic, elevated 3D view looking slightly down and to the left at the column of layers, capturing the vertical stacking and the curvature of the trajectory lines.
interactionPlan.view_reasoning: (1) The dominant vertical edges of the bounding box run straight up-down, while the horizontal plane boundaries project as parallel diagonals angling up-left and up-right. (2) This isometric-like projection implies a camera rotated roughly 45 degrees relative to the box faces (azimuth_deg = 45). (3) The top and bottom faces are clearly visible as flat diamond shapes rather than thin lines, which indicates a moderate look-down angle (elevation_deg = 35).

camera_view.view_notes: Perfect match for the isometric schematic layout. Maintains the vertical aspect ratio of the network stack while letting the user orbit to inspect how individual pathways cross or separate in intermediate layers.

inline_constraints.default_view: must match the original image silhouette, size, label scale, and crop
inline_constraints.visible_ui: at most 2 compact controls positioned near the bottom edge without a solid background panel
inline_constraints.explainers: hover tooltips on planes to identify layer depth, and click interactions to select/highlight a single trajectory
inline_constraints.framing: preserve the tall, vertical aspect ratio of the original figure with sufficient margins
inline_constraints.camera: must load with orthographic projection matching the source isometric sketch exactly

interactionPlan.notes: Render the trajectories as smooth 3D TubeGeometries. Let users click a specific path to dim the other paths, allowing them to trace a single data point's journey through the network layers. For the animated particles, animate small glowing spheres along the curves using a path parameter t that updates in the render loop.

phase2Evaluation.interactivity_usability_analysis: The developer implemented several high-quality, functional, and pedagogically useful interactions: (1) A 'Flow Direction' dropdown menu that reverses the visual direction of animated particle flow along trajectories and highlights corresponding side arrows (Forward/Backward). (3) Clickable 3D elements (trajectories) that isolate the selected path and dim others using 'registerInteractive'. (4) Interactive layer planes and side arrows that update the state on click. (5) A fully implemented step-through guided demo ('goToStep' wired to 'window.goToStep') with detailed narration steps for representation learning and generative modeling concepts.
phase2Evaluation.concept_accuracy_analysis: Core concept: The inverse relationship between representation learning (data to embedding) and generative modeling (embedding to data) viewed layer-by-layer in a deep neural network. User-visible claims: (1) 'Forward (Representation)' controls and text describe mapping concrete data upward to abstract embeddings layer-by-layer — accurate. (2) 'Backward (Generative)' controls and text describe mapping abstract concepts downward to concrete data — accurate. (3) Side arrows and text labeling 'Representation learning' (upward) and 'Generative modeling' (downward) — accurate representation of the inverse mappings. (4) Layer slices (Data, Layer 1, Layer 2, Embedding) showing intermediate levels of abstraction — accurate conceptual representation of neural net layers.
phase2Evaluation.notes: The figure is exceptionally well-implemented, achieving perfect scores in both concept accuracy and interactivity. It clearly and accurately illustrates the inverse relationship between representation learning and generative modeling using highly interactive layer planes, flow trajectories, and a comprehensive step-by-step guided demo.
